My friend bought this for me a while back and although we had played previously for some reason we just stopped. Jump forward to now and since we were bored a couple days back we decided to pick it back up, I have NO IDEA why we STOPPED playing. This game is FANTASTIC, the absolute chaos of hearing the screams of your soldiers mixed with voice lines that are so out of left field, SO many gun shots, the screeching of the monsters, the radio chatter, dismembered insect bodies flying everywhere, the discord call with your buddies, ALL while being covered in SO MANY bug guts that you should practically be drowning in them throughout the 110 missions of playtime is MESMERIZING.

Could I tell you what was happening in the story? Not at all. HOWEVER, I can tell you that the game is INCREDIBLY FUN!

I haven't played Single player mode but I can tell you that co-op with friends is an ABSOLUTE blast. THERE ARE 110 MISSIONS for you and your friends to play through so I believe the game is worth the price, but if you want to make the deal even sweeter you can get ALL of that for $23.99 when the game goes on sale. The game even though it is nothing like it reminds me of Starship Troopers (a movie that I adore, ignore the 2nd and 3rd movies because they are trash tho). I would HIGHLY recommend this game, honestly by this point we should work full time for the Black Diamond Pest Control.

Thanks, L.

[h1] EDF! EDF! EDF! [/h1]

TL;DR: You're a Japanese Starship Troopers throwing ICBMs at Bugs, Frogs, and Robots. Its the most stupid, ridiculous game I think I have ever played and its friggin amazing.

EDF is a game I have had my eye on for a long time, though I just recently considered buying this one in particular, citing some QoL changes that make it slightly more favorable than 4.1. In short, EDF is what happens when a game gives you WMDs and says, "Just go kill the things, there's different things that also show up kill them too kthx."

Gameplay is divided into 4 distinct classes: Ranger, Wing Diver, Air Raider (Raytheon), and Fencer. 

Ranger is more than likely the first you'll play. You are Guy with a F*cking gun, Savior of Humanity. You use Guns and Rockets to show those alien bastards that humanity's fascination with making small rocks travel at high speed wasn't a fruitless endeavor. This is where you'll find the most Starship Trooper-y feel from EDF. Shooting things full of holes until they stop moving, just as god intended.

Wing Diver is a class I don't actually play, mainly because I would rather have the ability to not instantly die If I'm so much as glared at, though the class is fairly mobile and has a suite of high tech plasma and laser weapons for you to make the aliens think they turned up to a planet-wide rave.

Air Raider channels the power of the United States military defense budget (The EDF is canonically HQed in North America) to lay waste to anything foolish enough to ignore the concept of a ceiling. He can come up with 735.5 billion ways to kill you so you best respect the tools he can bring to the table. Gunships, Vehicles, Satellite lasers, Cruise Missiles, and WMDs are all his kit and his alone. He has some limpet guns for closer range as well, but lets be honest: You aren't playing this class right if you aren't using a giant space laser as a Personal Defense Weapon.

Fencer is the "not-as-heavy-as-Air-Raider-but-still-pretty-heavy" weapon expert, his entire goal is to become a semi-truck filled with anvils and railroad anything that didn't sign the Geneva Convention (Spoiler: the Aliens didn't). As the only class that can wield two of the same weapon, you can sacrifice all of your mobility/defensive kit for the sake of pure. unadulterated. dakka. He is a difficult class to play (generally speaking compared to the other 3), but mastery of this class means you can make anything wake up in a cold sweat just thinking about you. You are *their* boogeyman.

All 4 classes are fun and distinct from one another and all 4 are viable, it really comes down to personal preference as to who you want to play as. Ranger would be your safest option in terms of simplicity, though.

Story is cheesy B-movie shenanigans with Voice acting that can be both great and "The Room" levels of terrible at the same time. It is merely a vessel for you to kill more aliens so I wouldn't think too hard about why aliens use things like giant insects and "Non-Descript, Non-Copyright Infringing Kaiju-Type Entity". As I said before, just go kill the thing! You get shiny for it so do it!

The game also supports local 2 player and Online 4 player Co-Op for the times when you and the boys want to stretch the definition of "Minimum Collateral Damage".

The game is stupid mayhem and I couldn't ask for anything more. Though the base price is steep it often goes on sale so watch for that. I also highly recommend you at least pay the *tiniest* bit of attention to the story because EDF 6, if and when it comes out on Steam, is a direct sequel.

Buy it and go kill things for shiny! EDF!
